subject: Re: Acme - feature parity & competitive eval follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acmecorp.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Acme - post-demo recap & next tests

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- What we heard: Acme needs predictable latency for customer-facing chat (P95 <= 250ms), structured output for downstream billing ingestion (JSON invoice schema), and robust function/tool-calling to orchestrate internal workflows. Also want to understand unit cost vs the hyperscalers for your expected 2M tokens/month.

- Redwood differentiators we highlighted:
  - Streaming + function/tool calling support out of the box (we can stream token-by-token while invoking webhook-based tools without blocking your UX).
  - Structured-output templates and schema validation to reduce post-processing errors.
  - Smart routing/quantization profiles to hit latency SLOs while lowering unit cost.

Proposed next tests (we can run these on hosted trial or a short Dedicated proof-of-concept):
1) Streaming function call test: end-to-end chat where model streams tokens and triggers a mock invoice-generator webhook. Measure P95 and end-to-end time-to-first-byte for the UI.
2) Structured output parity: send 500 sample invoices and compare Redwood vs Hyperscaler-A for schema accuracy (field extraction) and fallback behavior on malformed inputs.
3) Cost & throughput baseline: 1hr load window (burst profile you provided) to compare tokens/sec and per-token cost projections.

Attachments: I attached an evaluation matrix and notes comparing Redwood vs Hyperscaler-A and B — highlights in the PDF.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm which of the three tests you want first?
- Proposed timeslot for the streaming test: Mon 2027-01-11 16:00-17:00 ET. Rafael will run the test harness; Vivek will review SLOs and routing.

Thanks — talk soon.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Attachment: acme_evaluation_matrix.csv (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_notes.pdf (PDF summary)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2027 09:24:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Acme - post-demo recap & next tests

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Priya and I chatted and we're aligned on priorities. Quick answers: 

- Run the Streaming function call test first — that's our highest risk area for UX. We want to validate token-by-token streaming with a webhook that creates invoices. P95 target is 250ms; we'd accept an initial delta of +/-50ms in the POC.
- For structured output parity, please include the invoice schema we sent last quarter (I re-attached it here). We want precision/recall on line items and totals.
- Cost baseline: run the 1hr burst with the payloads we shared (burst_profile_v2.json).

Can Rafael and Vivek confirm they can run the harness Mon 16:00 ET? If not, provide alternate times this week. Also, include a quick checklist of what we need to instrument on our side (sample webhook, CORS for streaming endpoints, any auth tokens).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of ML Infrastructure | Acme Corp
jordan.lee@acmecorp.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 14:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Acme - post-demo recap & next tests

Jordan —

We can run the streaming function call test Mon 2027-01-11 16:00 ET as proposed. Quick tech notes and checklist for the test: 

Checklist for Acme (what we need from you):
- Sample invoice schema (JSON Schema) and 500 sample invoices (you mentioned you have a corpus — a subset of 500 is ideal).
- A mock invoice webhook endpoint that returns 200/201 for successful creations. If you prefer, we can deploy a short-lived mock on our infra and share the endpoint.
- CORS enabled if you plan to stream directly to a browser client during the demo.
- A temporary API key for Redwood to call any internal logging endpoint if you want us to post run artifacts (or we can share logs in the Drive link).

What Redwood will measure and report (deliverables):
- Token-by-token streaming latency (time-to-first-byte for the stream) and end-to-end P95.
- Function call invocation latency (time from trigger to 200 response), retry/failure behavior, and ordering guarantees.
- Structured output accuracy matrix (precision/recall per field) comparing Redwood vs Hyperscaler-A run on same inputs.
- Cost projection based on observed tokens/sec and model config.

Technical approach notes:
- We'll run two model configs: a quantized low-latency variant (to test cost/latency tradeoff) and a full-fidelity model for accuracy comparison.
- For streaming + function calling, Redwood will demonstrate streaming chunks while simultaneously emitting a function call with the parsed invoice JSON — this mimics your UI flow and avoids blocking.

I'll provision the harness and share a link to execution logs + result CSV to the Drive folder after the run.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.m@redwood.ai

Attachment: run_playbook.md (test harness notes)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Acme - post-demo recap & next tests (confirming SLOs)

Quick internal note — looping in Jordan for visibility. Rafael: please prioritize the streaming latency metric and ensure the quantized model maintains the invoice schema fidelity at >= 95% for required fields. If it falls below that threshold, include an automatic fallback to the full-fidelity variant in the harness so we can show a graceful degradation path.

Marissa: I'll join the call Mon and monitor routing policies to validate the smart fallback and autoscaling behavior. Rafael — please add a short blurb in the results that explains when/why we fall back (cost vs accuracy tradeoff).

Vivek
VP Product | Redwood Inference
vivek.k@redwood.ai
